43.title: The Jones Act of 1920
43.description: The Jones Act, Section 27 of the Merchant Marine Act (46 U.S.C. § 55102), prohibits the transport of merchandise by water between points in the United States in any vessel that is not U.S.-built, U.S.-owned, and U.S.-documented. In Puerto Rico's case, this drives up the price of nearly everything sold here, slowly strangling an island that once sustained itself.

49.title: Puerto Rico
49.description: Columbus named the island *San Juan Bautista*. *Puerto Rico* first referred only to a Spanish settlement on one of the Caribbean's best natural harbors. Positioned along the trade-wind route from Spain, it became one of the first major ports ships reached in the Americas, and Spain fortified it heavily with El Morro and San Cristóbal. As the port became the island's main point of contact with the world, sailors, merchants, and mapmakers began calling the whole island by its name. Over the 1500s, the names traded places, as the island became *Puerto Rico* and the city took *San Juan*.

80.title: Money
80.description: A widely accepted medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value. In the United States, the Federal Reserve issues the dollar and the Treasury prints and mints it. The dollar is backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government, the same government that passed $40 trillion in debt in August 2026 and now borrows to pay the interest on what it already owes.

83.title: Upkeep
83.description: A city is a cathedral of industry that never sleeps, and it does not mend itself. Beneath its spires and along its arteries, unseen laborers perform the endless rites of upkeep, patching iron veins, soothing tired machines, and holding back the slow tide of rust and ruin. Their work is never finished and rarely seen, yet without it, the great engine of the city would falter and fall silent.

132.description: Puerto Rico's Incentives Code was signed in 2019 to draw outside investment by offering new residents a 0% tax rate on capital gains, dividends, and interest. As wealthy investors buy homes along the coast, housing prices climb and locals are pushed out of the towns their families built.
